category: SURFACE N: production evidence (Sentry org qaren-rr, projects python-fastapi + react-native, last 14 days, read-only)
summary:
Every Sentry tool worked (org qaren-rr, region de.sentry.io; projects python-fastapi, react-native, booking-os-web). There were no auth errors. The production signal is very thin, and that is by design:
- The backend sends only ERROR log lines to Sentry.
- Deliberate 503s (TIMEOUT / LLM_UNAVAILABLE) are dropped, and 4xx responses (INSUFFICIENT_DATA, "<2 products") are never captured.
- Image-tier failures log at WARNING/INFO.
- Client image onError has no telemetry.
- Traces are sampled at 10%: about 1,400-2,100 backend spans a day are discarded client-side, against 0-253 kept.
- The Sentry Logs dataset is empty.

In 14 days: python-fastapi has 4 issues and 65 error events. react-native has 0 errors; its only events are 27 info-level `comparison_wall_time` telemetry messages.

The tester videos still line up exactly with production telemetry, because each RPReplay filename is the Unix time the recording was saved.
- **V02 (12:49:34-12:50:25Z):** PYTHON-FASTAPI-1X fired 4 times (12:50:05 and 12:50:15, two attempts x two URLs). fragrancex.com answered 403 (span status permission_denied) to the backend fetch of a real product page (/products/calvin-klein/obsession-perfume). So V02 failed because fragrancex blocks Railway. It was not homepage acceptance, at least for that field. This matters for the user's "ingest all of fragrancex" request.
- **V09 (13:43:42-13:44:23Z):** trace 5915a2b6 shows compare_urls returning 200 in 7.1 s with 3 LLM calls, then rpc/increment_lifetime_comparisons. A two-"Unknown Product" result went down the success branch: the credit was kept, the lifetime counter bumped and a history row saved. This confirms MYEZ-002/005/011/012/027 in production.
- **V01 and V06 (camera):** client wall time to first card was 40,032 ms and 39,519 ms, matching the audit's ~40 s. Sampled backend text compares all ran 30.5-34.8 s, at or over the 30 s cap, and client text compares had a median of 32.7 s (n=7).

The client wall-time instrumentation is itself broken for the URL and camera paths: start() is only called on the text path.

Other production signals: Serper failed about 45% of sampled calls (p95 16.9 s), Bright Data returned 401 from 10-09 to 10-11, and the L2 product cache (product_specs / product_reviews) misses with 4xx. Simple routes take 2.6-8.4 s, which points to event-loop stalls.

The defects behind the user's three complaints (camera misidentification, missing images, missing info) have no direct Sentry signal at all. V04 and V07 left zero telemetry.

findings.title: Sentry can structurally not see most tester-visible defect classes; production silence is not health

evidence.note: LoggingIntegration(level=logging.ERROR): only ERROR log lines become breadcrumbs/events

failed_request_status_codes excludes 503, and _before_send drops any event with response status 503 (TIMEOUT, FEATURE_DISABLED, LLM_UNAVAILABLE surfaces); 4xx (INSUFFICIENT_DATA 400, '<2 products' 400, NOT_A_PDP) are never captured
traces_sample_rate=0.1; init has no enable_logs, so the Sentry Logs dataset is empty (search_logs over 14d returned no rows)
client tracesSampleRate 0.1; search_traces returned zero react-native transactions in 14d
client_discard/sample_rate drops of 1,143-2,071 spans per day vs 0-253 accepted per day; errors dataset: only 3 client_discard network_error drops (error data is complete)
python-fastapi 65 error events in 7 message/transaction groups; react-native 27 events, all level=info message comparison_wall_time, 0 errors/crashes in 90d

findings.detail: The backend Sentry stream only contains logger.error lines (provider ConnectTimeout, Bright Data 401, URL fetch failure) and 500s. The defect classes the audit is about cannot reach Sentry: TIMEOUT/LLM_UNAVAILABLE (503, dropped), INSUFFICIENT_DATA and URL '<2 products' (400, never captured), and Unknown-Product or misidentified results (HTTP 200 success). The same goes for image misses (image_service logs WARNING/INFO), client image load errors (no telemetry), and SSE fallback (breadcrumb only, which rides on no event because RN has zero errors). Transactions are 10% sampled, so per-route p50/p95 rests on 1-5 sampled traces. No /api/v1/image/* transaction was sampled in 30 days. Any 'no signal found' row below therefore means 'not observable', not 'not happening'.

findings.title: V02 fragrancex failure = fragrancex returns HTTP 403 to the Railway fetch of a real product page (PYTHON-FASTAPI-1X)

evidence.file: Sentry PYTHON-FASTAPI-1X (events 45dbe359, 214cf269 at 2026-10-18T12:50:05Z; f3ff0b9c, e3c59f2e at 12:50:15Z), trace 2e59ae38aca04795883c6c9306de3495, release 683f56c0, client MYEZ 3 iOS
evidence.note: 4 events, first 12:50:05.062Z, last 12:50:15Z, 'Failed to fetch URL host www.fragrancex.com: HTTPStatusError', culprit app.api.url_routes.compare_urls; the http.client span context has status permission_denied (=403) and description 'GET https://www.fragrancex.com/products/calvin-klein/obsession-perfume'
epoch 1792327825 = 2026-10-18T12:50:25Z (save time); window 12:49:34-12:50:25Z; the audit's failure at 00:32-00:43 = 12:50:06-12:50:17Z, matching the two error bursts (two Compare taps x two URLs)

fetch_page does raise_for_status, logs host + exception type at ERROR and returns None; extract_from_url returns success False 'Failed to fetch URL'; compare_from_urls returns 'Could not extract both products'
the non-success exit refunds the credit and raises a code-less HTTP 400 with no reason code, so the client cannot tell 'store blocked us' from 'not a product page'

findings.detail: The audit (MYEZ-005) read V02's fields as the fragrancex homepage. Production shows at least one field was a real PDP (Calvin Klein Obsession), and both fields failed with 403 twice. The likely cause is bot protection on fragrancex against the plain httpx fetch from Railway's IP (inferred; the 403 status itself is measured). The credit was refunded, so V02 did not burn quota. The user-visible 'retry' dialog maps to the code-less 400 (MYEZ-006). This bears directly on the user's request to 'add all fragrancex product data to our database': the existing direct-fetch path cannot read fragrancex from production. Any catalog pre-load needs a different, permitted channel, and robots/ToS must be checked first.

findings.detail: This is the clearest production confirmation in the audit set. A URL compare that produced two 'Unknown Product' cards and a green winner returned 200. It billed the user (the credit reserved at the gate was not refunded and the lifetime counter was incremented) and wrote a history row. That covers MYEZ-002, 005, 011, 012 and 027. With ENABLE_SEARCH_LOG_TRUTH ON, its search_logs row is written with success=True (url_routes.py:206-211), so admin error stats count it as a success too. The V09 RN event in the same trace (13:46:20Z, first_card 0, ready_celebration 805, user_tappable 1,246) carries no information about the compare duration. A PDP classifier already exists behind ENABLE_NOT_A_PDP_FILTER but is not reachable from /url/compare.

findings.detail: The audit's 38-42 s scan waits (MYEZ-015) match the client telemetry for V01 (40.0 s) and V06 (39.5 s). The consistent ~40 s camera value suggests the camera compare also runs to the 30 s cap after a few seconds of vision and upload (inferred). Compares that end at the cap deliver partial data: empty spec rows, missing prices, missing images (MYEZ-003/010/014/022; inferred link, consistent with the S78 diagnosis). Backend p50/p95 rests on only 4 sampled text compares and 0 camera compares, so the client wall-time numbers are the better (if flawed, see next finding) production measure.

findings.detail: Telemetry cannot currently produce honest scan or URL p50/p95. Camera values are only usable by accident: ResultsScreen's 800 ms reveal timer seeds t0 at mount. URL values are stale. Some compares emit nothing at all (V04, V07); the cause is unknown, possibly the SDK Dedupe integration or app backgrounding (inferred). The audit's acceptance test for MYEZ-015 (scan_start / identity_resolved / comparison_ready timings) has no event types to land in (see the analytics finding). findings.detail: ConnectTimeout issue 1R stopped after the 2026-10-11 22:50 off-loop flip, but 1Q (Serper shopping) recurred on 2026-10-14. Sampled Serper spans still failed on 10-14. internal_error on these httpx spans is most likely asyncio cancellation at the compare cap or timeouts (inferred). Serper is the search backbone and the Tier-1 image source (image_service.py:255-271), so its failure rate plausibly drives missing prices, specs and images (MYEZ-010/014/003; inferred). No firecrawl, scrapedo or zyte span or error appeared in 14 days of sampled data. Either those providers were not on the sampled paths, or their flags are off (not determined here).

findings.title: Image misses (MYEZ-014) and camera misidentification (MYEZ-001) leave no production trace by construction

evidence.note: every image tier failure or miss logs WARNING or INFO ('All tiers exhausted ... returning None' is INFO), so it never reaches Sentry
image_url is a Phase-1 race with a 5.0 s bound (Serper Images + Tier-3 GPT fallback); the price page image is used only if present
onError={() => setErrored(true)}: no Sentry capture and no trackEvent

ERROR only on vision exception / parse error / compare exception (0 events in 90d); identified names logged at INFO; no confidence gate in the 330-440 block (vision returns confidence high/medium/low, openai_service.py:144, 221)
every photo is transcoded on device to JPEG, 1024 px wide, quality 0.8, before upload, so HEIC never reaches the server
32 issues in 90d, none for image/vision/identify/HEIC

findings.detail: The user's two camera complaints ('AI can't spot products' and 'pictures sometimes missing') have zero production signal. That is because nothing at ERROR level or above is emitted, not because they don't happen. V04 (watch/violin) left no error, trace or wall-time event. The camera path turns vision output into a 'brand name vs brand name' text query (image_routes.py:440-450) with no confidence gate. A low-confidence or wrong read is therefore resolved through text search, which is the MYEZ-001 mechanism (inferred). Measuring image coverage or identification quality needs new additive telemetry (see recommendations).

findings.title: Event-loop stall signal: trivial routes take 2.6-8.4 s; health_check p95 8.4 s

evidence.note: health_check ~490 extrapolated (~49 sampled) p50 6 ms but p95 8,372 ms; feedback track_events p50 736 ms, p95 8,442 ms; usage_status p50 4,164 ms; home_smart_pick p50 6,665 ms; update_push_token p50 7,265 ms; referral status p50 1,745 ms
health_check 2,665 ms; usage_status 4,266 ms and home_savings 4,944 ms whose child http.client spans sum to under 0.8 s
4,310 extrapolated spans, p50 289 ms, p95 1,537 ms (Redis REST round trips)
'Stay OFF: ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD, ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD ...'

findings.detail: Large gaps between transaction wall time and child-span time on routes that only do a few Supabase/Upstash calls indicate requests queued behind blocking work on the single uvicorn loop (inferred). This is consistent with sync supabase-py and Upstash calls staying on the loop while ENABLE_SYNC_DB_OFFLOAD and ENABLE_ASYNC_REDIS_OFFLOAD are OFF. It adds seconds to every screen load around a compare. It is not a single-defect cause for the 40 s scans, which are dominated by the 30 s compare cap.

findings.title: L2 product knowledge cache ('brain') misses: product_specs / product_reviews reads fail 4xx inside compares

evidence.file: Sentry search_traces span.domain supabase.co status invalid_argument (14d)
evidence.note: GET /rest/v1/product_specs 30 and GET /rest/v1/product_reviews 30 extrapolated (about 3 sampled each), all in text_compare_get, 2026-10-14 03:50-04:26Z, p50 381 ms
get_cached_specs / get_cached_reviews use .eq('product_key', ...).single(); any exception (a miss included) is swallowed at logger.debug; TTL 30 days specs / 14 days reviews

findings.detail: The 4xx is most likely PostgREST's no-rows response to .single(), which Sentry maps to invalid_argument; I did not measure this on the pinned supabase-py/sentry-sdk (inferred). If so, the cached product tables had no row for the products compared on 10-14, and each miss costs a ~380 ms round trip on the loop. This is the existing landing place for the user's 'brain' request: specs and reviews are already cached per product_key in product_specs / product_reviews (prices in product_prices). A pre-ingested catalog would be served from here, but it must use the same product_key normalisation to hit.

findings.title: What the app already records about failed compares (code only, no DB access)

evidence.note: search_logs row = query, input_type, products_found, success, cost, duration_ms, user_id, error_message, is_synthetic (only with ENABLE_SEARCH_LOG_SYNTHETIC_MARKER); no fields for winner, Unknown Product, image coverage, spec coverage or identity confidence
item 5: 'ENABLE_SEARCH_LOG_TRUTH=true is confirmed on web', so url failure/success rows (url_routes.py:145-213) and camera failure rows (image_routes.py:509-616) are written
admin get_error_stats = error rate + top error_message from search_logs.success=False; V09-style Unknown-Product deliveries count as successes

user_events allowlist = funnel/share/onboarding/spec_expand/result_abandon/screenshot/result_view_duration/compare_cancelled; no compare_failed, image_load_failed, identity_dispute, scan_start, identity_resolved or comparison_ready type
the feedback card always submits useful: true plus a chip (accurate / detailed / fast; allowlisted at feedback_routes.py:44-47); there is no negative or 'wrong product' channel

findings.detail: Failed compares are recorded only in search_logs, server side. URL '<2 products' failures carry 'Could not extract both products', and camera unsuccessful results carry the failure message. A misleading 'success' (Unknown Product, wrong identity, empty specs, missing images) is recorded as success=True with products_found names. comparison_feedback can only ever say 'useful' (MYEZ-023 confirmed in code), so no production dataset exists for identity disputes or 'not useful'. The tester session rows should exist in search_logs for 2026-10-18 12:43-13:47Z; an owner-run query could confirm them (not run here, no DB access).

findings.title: Side finding: error-event trace context ships the user-pasted outbound URL path to Sentry

evidence.note: contexts.trace.description = 'GET https://www.fragrancex.com/products/calvin-klein/obsession-perfume' (a full user URL path)
U8d R8/UG2 intent: 'the user's URL path and query never reach the log line (and so Sentry)'
_outbound_description path-stripping runs on transaction spans only; _before_send runs only the secret-pattern scrub (_scrub_dict) over contexts

findings.detail: This is low impact here because the URL is a public product page, but it contradicts the stated U8d rule that user URL paths never reach Sentry. A user-pasted URL with a path token would leak the same way. The fix is additive: apply _outbound_description to contexts.trace.description in _before_send. It is not related to the audit defects.

recommendations: Treat 'no Sentry signal' as 'not observable', not 'healthy'. Before building any fix for MYEZ-001/003/014 the session needs production measurement it does not have. Have the owner run read-only SQL on search_logs for 2026-10-18 12:40-13:50Z, plus a 14-day input_type x success x error_message breakdown, to size the URL and camera failure mix. No agent should touch the DB or Railway.

Additive backend telemetry behind a NEW dark flag (none exists: the grep of all ENABLE_* names in app/ found no compare-quality telemetry flag; ENABLE_SEARCH_LOG_TRUTH is ON but carries no quality fields). At each delivery exit, emit one PII-free Sentry info message per compare (the comparison_wall_time pattern) or log line. Tags: input_type, unknown_product_count, winner_emitted, image_url_present per product, spec_rows_filled, price_present, vision confidence, cap_hit. This makes MYEZ-002/003/014 measurable without touching the frozen response contract.

Turn on traces for the paths that matter without raising global volume: a traces_sampler behind a dark flag that samples /api/v1/image/identify, /api/v1/url/compare and the text compare at 1.0 and everything else at 0.1. Today there are 0 camera transactions in 30 days and only 4 text compares in 14 days.

URL path (MYEZ-002/005/006/012/027): reuse the existing ENABLE_NOT_A_PDP_FILTER classifier (price_service.py:12940-12990), which today is not reachable from /url/compare. Do it behind a new default-OFF flag in url_extraction_service.compare_from_urls. Treat 'Unknown Product' / no title / homepage as a non-delivery (refund, no lifetime bump, no history row) through the existing failure exit (url_routes.py:171-197), so the build-3 client sees an already-handled 400 shape. Pass the fetch status (403 vs not-a-PDP) only in log or telemetry fields, not in the frozen response.

For the user's 'ingest all of fragrancex' request: production proves fragrancex returns 403 to the backend's direct fetch from Railway (PYTHON-FASTAPI-1X, span permission_denied). Do not plan a scrape over the existing fetch_page path. Check robots/ToS and look for a permitted feed or affiliate channel first. Land the data in the existing L2 tables (product_specs 30-day TTL, product_reviews 14-day TTL, product_prices) using the same product_key normalisation the compare uses, or it will never hit.

L2 cache reads: switch the .single() lookups in product_data_service.py:205-212 and 369-376 to a zero-row-safe form (maybe_single / limit(1)). Measure the pinned supabase-py behaviour first (memory rule), because each miss currently costs a 4xx round trip on the loop. Byte-identical results; it can ship unflagged only if a test proves a miss returns None both ways.

Client (post-approval only; no OTA before App Review approval): (a) call getWallTimeTracker().start() in runUrlCompare and in the camera identify path, and reset `started` in report(); (b) add an image_load_failed event (new VALID_EVENT_TYPES entry, widen-only) from ProductImage onError; (c) add a negative or 'wrong product' feedback path, since FeedbackCard always sends useful:true. Server-side allowlist widening (feedback_routes.py:58-90) is additive and can land first.
